paragraph_revisions.old: Seasonal surface-water decline and limits to drought assessment in northwestern Bangladesh
paragraph_revisions.new: Mapped seasonal surface water decline under changing observation support in northwestern Bangladesh

paragraph_revisions.old: Surface-water monitoring can inform climate-resilient water management only when changes in mapped water are distinguished from changes in observation support. We assessed annual seasonal and permanent surface-water source classes in Naogaon, Chapainawabganj and Rajshahi, northwestern Bangladesh, using Joint Research Centre water histories and gridded climate data. The primary analysis covered 2000–2021 on a fixed, retrospectively selected, annually observed footprint of 1,276.41 km²; 2000–2024 results were retained as a source-version sensitivity. Separate 2015–2024 Sentinel-1 and Dynamic World analyses examined threshold sensitivity, paired support and drought-recovery identifiability. A stratified four-month comparison retained all 720 sampled pixel-months, including unresolved references. Seasonal source-class area declined from 938.53 to 699.91 km² between 2000 and 2021, a decrease of 25.42%. Negative seasonal time coefficients persisted in Naogaon and Rajshahi after adjustment for annual climate, observation effort and a 2016 processing-boundary indicator, whereas the corresponding Chapainawabganj interval included zero. Permanent source-class area increased by 41.04% between the endpoints, but its adjusted time-coefficient intervals included zero after the processing-boundary control. Increasing the Dynamic World confidence threshold from 0.5 to 0.7 raised conditional radar–optical agreement from 89.04% to 98.71%, while mean paired support fell from 11.07% to 3.29% of the separate analysis footprint. Assisted dated interpretation assigned comparison labels to 76.54% of design-weighted sampled area-time; conditional agreement was 98.56%, without establishing independent accuracy. Recovery duration remained unidentified in all nine support/reference specifications. These results support targeted investigation of declining seasonal water in the retained footprint and show why agreement, spatial support and temporal continuity should be reported together before using satellite products to assess drought resilience. The analysis does not estimate district-wide water storage, validate annual hydroperiod classes independently or attribute residual changes to groundwater abstraction.
paragraph_revisions.new: Changes in satellite-mapped water can inform climate-resilient management only when observation support is explicit. We assessed annual seasonal and permanent water source classes in Naogaon, Chapainawabganj and Rajshahi, northwestern Bangladesh, using JRC histories and gridded climate data. The primary 2000–2021 analysis used a retrospectively selected, annually observed footprint of 1,276.41 km². Exploratory reanalysis compared seven footprint/validity cohorts, multi-year windows, simpler climate models, approximate uncertainty estimates and chronological hindcasts. Seasonal source-class area fell from 938.53 to 699.91 km² between the endpoints (25.42%); comparison of the first and final five-year means gave a smaller decline of 14.70%. A footprint based on water observed in 2000–2004 and annual validity through 2021 gave an 18.79% five-year decline. Negative seasonal coefficients persisted across the tested models, although interval and district support varied. Permanent-class gains were sensitive to observation and processing controls. Static river and 2020 cropland context separated contrasting mapped trajectories without identifying their causes. During 2015–2024, raising the Dynamic World threshold from 0.5 to 0.7 increased conditional radar–optical agreement from 89.04% to 98.71%, while mean paired support fell from 11.07% to 3.29%; wet-season support was particularly sparse. Assisted interpretation of 720 sampled pixel-months assigned 76.54% of design-weighted area-time, with 98.56% conditional agreement but no independent accuracy estimate. No actual drought-recovery duration was identified under nine support/reference specifications. Synthetic pulse diagnostics retaining real gaps and envelope widths also failed to confirm the tested deficits. The results identify a restricted-footprint seasonal decline and the observation requirements for investigating it; district-wide water storage, causal abstraction effects and independently validated resilience remain unmeasured.

paragraph_revisions.old: This range permits arbitrary agreement or disagreement for unresolved labels. It bounds completion of the proxy comparison, not physical-water accuracy. Approximate sampling intervals used 2,000 pixel-month bootstrap replicates within the original strata, with seed 20261016. These intervals omit reference, timing, radiometric, registration and spatial-clustering errors. Degenerate conditional bootstrap intervals were left unavailable rather than presented as certainty.
paragraph_revisions.new: This range permits arbitrary agreement or disagreement for unresolved labels. It bounds completion of the proxy comparison, not physical-water accuracy. Approximate sampling intervals used 2,000 pixel-month percentile bootstrap replicates within the original strata, with seed 20261016. No finite-population correction or spatial-cluster model was used. These intervals exclude reference, timing, radiometric, registration and spatial-clustering errors and do not resolve nonrandom reference failure. Degenerate conditional bootstrap intervals remained unavailable rather than being presented as certainty.

paragraph_revisions.old: The completed computational audit verified 9,393 source-file checksums and reconciled the downloaded export inventories and reported numerical tables. The active analysis retains the corrected dated-label version and its history. Manuscript preparation read these frozen results without refitting the scientific models. Figure inputs, table copies and their SHA-256 hashes are recorded separately. The analysis environment used Python 3.12, NumPy 2.3.5, pandas 2.3.3, statsmodels 0.14.5 and rasterio 1.5.0. Software checks establish reproducibility properties; they do not establish environmental accuracy. The overall design is exploratory, and results were known when the final restricted scope was documented.
paragraph_revisions.new: The original computational audit verified 9,393 source-file checksums and reconciled export inventories. The revision additionally rechecked all fifty annual/monthly source rasters, reconstructed the original annual summaries to within 10⁻⁶ km², and reran the explicitly frozen exploratory models. The corrected dated-label version and its history were unchanged. Protocols, source versions, output tables, failed fits and SHA-256 manifests accompany the code. An initial calendar-gap bootstrap implementation was corrected before the reported outputs were frozen; superseded intervals are excluded. The environment used Python 3.12, NumPy 2.3.5, pandas 2.3.3, statsmodels 0.14.5 and rasterio 1.5.0. Computational checks do not establish environmental accuracy or confirmatory inference.

paragraph_revisions.old: The corresponding strict-majority transition map is shown in Figure 3. It distinguishes stable classes, gains, losses and seasonal/permanent transitions while preserving ambiguous windows; the mapped classes do not establish a physical mechanism.
paragraph_revisions.new: Figure 3 separates gross majority-class transitions from static landscape context. Among pixels with a majority in both windows, 264.1 km² moved from seasonal to nonwater and 110.1 km² from nonwater to seasonal; seasonal-to-permanent and permanent-to-seasonal transitions were 29.2 and 32.8 km². A further 11.04 km² lacked a strict majority in at least one window. At the 500 m river buffer, the change in five-year mean seasonal area was −64.49 km² near mapped rivers, −89.74 km² in more distant 2020 cropland and +19.84 km² in the remaining distant area. Their initial seasonal-area changes were −15.46%, −26.91% and +12.12%. Across the 200–1,000 m buffers, the respective percentage ranges were −15.54 to −15.25, −27.82 to −26.12 and +7.22 to +20.62. The partition changes with buffer distance; neither these ranges nor source-class transitions establish causes.

paragraph_revisions.old: The annual seasonal climate model also had limited predictive benefit. Mean fold RMSE was higher than the training-only mean benchmark in every district and the union. For the union, model RMSE was 0.0898 of footprint fraction, compared with 0.0862 for the benchmark. Permanent-class mean fold errors were lower than the corresponding benchmarks, but only three annual folds were available in each case. Climate-adjusted associations should therefore be interpreted without a general claim of improved prediction. Full coefficients, fold summaries and the separate 2000–2024 sensitivity are provided in Supplementary Data.
paragraph_revisions.new: The new models and matched-fold aggregation changed the hindcast comparison. Union seasonal pooled RMSE was 0.0745 for the monsoon model versus 0.0899 for the mean and 0.0628 for the trend benchmark on six test years. The reduced controlled model gave 0.0486 versus matched mean/trend errors of 0.1039/0.0726 on four years. Adding antecedent rainfall gave 0.0458, while the original full-control specification gave 0.0691 on those four years. These small, differing test sets limit generalization. The original climate-only analysis and its mean-of-fold-RMSE summaries remain archived and are distinct from this matched-fold pooled comparison.

paragraph_revisions.old: Figure 5 places the observed class areas beside the baseline fixed-climate model expectations. The smooth expected curves are model-derived summaries, not replacement observations or validation of the class assignments. Their interpretation remains subject to the processing and observation sensitivities in Figure 4.
paragraph_revisions.new: Figure 5 compares the footprint, time-window, equal-calendar support and hindcast sensitivities. On C1, the first-to-final three- and five-year seasonal changes were −14.28% and −14.70%, compared with −25.42% for endpoints. The five-year decrease was −18.79% on C4 and −19.72% on C5; C6 lacked sufficient coverage for a five-year comparison. All accepted primary seasonal point coefficients were negative across the tested cohorts/models, but their intervals and dependence preclude treating them as independent confirmations. Only November retained at least 20% of the union baseline-water footprint under the 22-year same-calendar rule (25.35%); June–October retained none. Equalizing calendar-month support therefore did not yield a representative complete annual cycle.

paragraph_revisions.old: Figure 8 shows both endpoints for all three districts and all three historical cohorts, including intervals crossing zero. This retains the unsupported combinations alongside the highlighted Rajshahi result.
paragraph_revisions.new: Seasonal support and class-specific diagnostics are shown in Figure 8. At thresholds 0.5 and 0.7, mean paired support during June–September was only 0.313% and 0.110% of the union historical-water cohort, versus 16.45% and 4.87% in other months. A bounded November 2024 score-stage probe examined one land-context area and three stable-source-water interiors. Maximum raw water scores were 0.619 and 0.753, respectively, and monthly-median maxima were 0.506 and 0.748; neither probe retained threshold-0.8 support. These selected areas cannot establish a domain-wide probability ceiling or rule out every processing error. The dated assisted comparison also differed between water and nonwater agreement, particularly in Naogaon. Neither diagnostic is an independent accuracy assessment. Full radar model and joint-cell tables retain unsupported combinations.

paragraph_revisions.old: The seasonal source class contracted within the fixed annual footprint. Its direction persisted in the union, and the climate/observation/processing sensitivity retained negative district coefficients in Naogaon and Rajshahi. This combination supports prioritizing those retained areas for closer hydrological and land-management investigation. The smaller Chapainawabganj endpoint decrease and its final interval spanning zero argue against applying one uniform district-level trend claim to the entire region.
paragraph_revisions.new: The mapped seasonal decline is supported by more than the choice of two endpoint years, but its magnitude depends on the comparison. The original endpoint decrease was 25.42%, whereas five-year means gave 14.70% on the original footprint and 18.79% on the baseline-water complete cohort. Whole-series associations and these window comparisons support investigating seasonal source-class contraction within retained areas. They do not justify one district-wide loss percentage. District uncertainty also matters: the controlled seasonal models retained clearer evidence in Naogaon and Rajshahi than in Chapainawabganj.

paragraph_revisions.old: Climate adjustment addressed a limited statistical question: how annual class shares co-varied with time after the specified weather and observation terms were included. The short annual series, approximate uncertainty estimates and seasonal hindcast performance constrain its use. Seasonal models did not outperform a training-only mean in average fold RMSE, despite retaining negative time coefficients in parts of the study area. This combination supports reporting associations while avoiding a claim that the model provides an improved operational forecast.
paragraph_revisions.new: Climate adjustment addressed a limited associational question. The monsoon model improved on its matched mean benchmark but not its trend benchmark; reduced observation/processing models improved on both on only four test years. Those results neither establish robust forecasting skill nor identify a climatic or management cause. Approximate HAC and residual-block intervals, leave-one-year-out fits and simpler specifications expose sensitivity; they cannot compensate for a short series or an imperfect observation process.

paragraph_revisions.old: Seasonal JRC source-class area declined by 25.42% between 2000 and 2021 within a fixed 1,276.41 km² annual-observation footprint in northwestern Bangladesh. Negative seasonal time associations persisted in Naogaon and Rajshahi after the specified climate, observation-effort and processing-boundary controls. Permanent-class endpoint gains were sensitive to the processing control and do not establish a robust continuing increase.
paragraph_revisions.new: Mapped seasonal JRC source-class area decreased within the retained annual-observation footprint in northwestern Bangladesh. The 2000–2021 endpoint decline was 25.42%, compared with 14.70% between five-year means on the same footprint and 18.79% on a baseline-water complete cohort. Negative seasonal associations persisted across the tested specifications, with stronger controlled district evidence in Naogaon and Rajshahi. Permanent-class endpoint gains remained sensitive to observation and processing controls. These findings concern classified areas and declared spatial support, not district-wide water storage.

paragraph_revisions.old: Derived results and complete comparison/support tables accompany the manuscript as Supplementary Data. The four v0.2.0-review archives—Supplementary Code, Supplementary Data Tables, Supplementary Data Grid and Supplementary Data Context—contain analysis code, genuine exported/aggregated inputs, result tables, metadata and checksums. They support statistical replay without GitHub access; full raw-pixel processing is not repeated. Public source products are identified in Table 1; exact assets are retained in Supplementary Methods, Section S1. The full source-raster history and dated image crops are not duplicated. Development materials are stored in the private GitHub repository https://github.com/asifahamed11/northwestern-bangladesh-surface-water; access is restricted to authorized GitHub accounts.
paragraph_revisions.new: Derived tables, revision protocols, source ledgers and analysis code accompany this revision. The original v0.2.0-review archives retain the earlier statistical replay and are explicitly distinguished from the new revision outputs; they alone do not reproduce the updated models and figures. The revision supplement records the new cohort summaries, model outputs, context and simulated diagnostics, with hashes and execution instructions. Full raw raster histories, large third-party source downloads and dated image crops are not duplicated. Product versions and restrictions are listed in Table 1 and Supplementary Methods. Development materials are stored in the private repository https://github.com/asifahamed11/northwestern-bangladesh-surface-water; access is restricted to authorized accounts. Private repository availability does not by itself satisfy public data-access requirements.
